source_evidence.observation: The analysis uses fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for op in {+, -, *, /}, where u is the unit roundoff. The paper states that this model is violated on machines lacking a guard digit and explicitly assumes that no floating-point underflows occur.

source_evidence.anchor: opening of section 2, error definition, and equation (2.1)
source_evidence.observation: The inputs x_1,...,x_n are real scalar numbers, the exact sum is S_n = sum_{i=1}^n x_i, the floating-point result is S_hat_n, and the forward error is E_n = S_hat_n - S_n.
If |delta_i| <= u for i = 1,...,m, then product_{i=1}^m (1 + delta_i) = 1 + theta_m with |theta_m| <= m u/(1 - m u) = gamma_m.

source_evidence.anchor: equation (2.6) and the relative-error display immediately following it
source_evidence.observation: For recursive summation, the ordering-independent absolute bound is |E_n| <= gamma_{n-1} sum_i |x_i|, and it is rewritten as |S_hat_n - S_n|/|S_n| <= gamma_{n-1} R_n, where R_n = sum_i |x_i|/|S_n|.

source_evidence.anchor: paragraph immediately after the relative-error display following equation (2.6)
source_evidence.observation: The paper states that when x_i >= 0 for every i, R_n = 1 and the relative-error bound is of order n u; when substantial cancellation makes sum_i |x_i| much larger than |sum_i x_i|, a small relative error cannot be guaranteed.

Pairwise summation, also called cascade summation, sums adjacent inputs in pairs and recursively repeats the process on the resulting sums. For the error-bound derivation the paper explicitly assumes, for simplicity, that n = 2^r, so every addend participates in log_2 n additions.
For power-of-two n, the computed pairwise result has the pathwise representation S_hat_n = sum_{i=1}^n x_i product_{k=1}^{log_2 n}(1 + delta_k^(i)), with |delta_k^(i)| <= u.

The main pairwise bound is |E_n| <= gamma_{log_2 n} sum_{i=1}^n |x_i|. The paper says this improves on the ordering-independent recursive bound (2.6) in its log_2 n rather than n dependence, while warning that the sharper order-dependent recursive bound (2.5) can be smaller in special cases.

binders: A number n of scalar summands and real inputs x_1,...,x_n are considered; n is implicitly a positive integer because it counts the inputs. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 784, opening of section 2]
For the derivation of the pairwise bound, n is restricted to n = 2^r; r is implicitly an integer and r = log_2 n. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, paragraph preceding equation (3.6)]

The unit roundoff u and the per-addition relative errors delta_k^(i) are associated with the floating-point computation, with i = 1,...,n and k = 1,...,log_2 n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 784, equation (1.2); PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, relation preceding equation (3.6)]
hypotheses: The computed result is produced by recursive pairwise/cascade summation, not by left-to-right recursive summation or a compensated method. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, pairwise-summation definition]
For equation (3.6), n = 2^r, so the reduction tree is balanced and every input encounters exactly r = log_2 n rounded additions. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, paragraph preceding equation (3.6)]

Each floating-point addition obeys the standard relative-error model with an error of magnitude at most u. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 784, equation (1.2); PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, relation preceding equation (3.6)]
No floating-point underflow occurs. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 784, paragraph following equation (1.2)]

The nonnegative relative-error consequence additionally requires x_i >= 0 for all i and S_n != 0; the latter is implicit because relative error and R_n divide by |S_n|. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 785, relative-error display and following paragraph]
conclusions: The computed pairwise sum satisfies S_hat_n = sum_{i=1}^n x_i product_{k=1}^{log_2 n}(1 + delta_k^(i)), where every |delta_k^(i)| <= u. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, unnumbered relation preceding equation (3.6)]
Its absolute forward error satisfies the exact gamma bound |S_hat_n - S_n| = |E_n| <= gamma_{log_2 n} sum_{i=1}^n |x_i|. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, equation (3.6)]

Combining equation (3.6) with the paper's nonnegative-input observation gives the inferred consequence |S_hat_n - S_n|/|S_n| <= gamma_{log_2 n} when all x_i >= 0 and S_n > 0. This pairwise relative form is not separately displayed in the paper. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 785, relative-error display and following paragraph; PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, equation (3.6)]

The source claims improvement only over the ordering-independent recursive bound's worst-case n dependence; it explicitly does not claim that pairwise summation always has a smaller bound than every ordering of recursive summation. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, paragraph following equation (3.6)]
definitions_and_conventions: S_n = sum_{i=1}^n x_i is the exact real sum, S_hat_n is the computed floating-point sum, and E_n = S_hat_n - S_n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 784, opening of section 2 and error definition]

gamma_m is defined by gamma_m = m u/(1 - m u), through the finite-product estimate product_i(1 + delta_i) = 1 + theta_m with |theta_m| <= gamma_m. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 784, unnumbered display after equation (2.2)]
R_n = sum_i |x_i|/|S_n| is the relative condition factor used when an absolute summation bound is divided by |S_n|. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 785, relative-error display following equation (2.6)]

Pairwise/cascade summation recursively replaces adjacent pairs by their sums; for odd-length intermediate lists the unpaired final entry is carried into the next list, although equation (3.6) is derived only under n = 2^r. contract_plain_english: For n = 2^r real scalar inputs, form the computed sum by repeatedly adding adjacent pairs in floating-point arithmetic. Under the standard relative-error model and with no underflow, every input passes through exactly log_2 n rounded additions, so the computed result differs from the exact sum by at most gamma_{log_2 n} times sum_i |x_i|, where gamma_m = m u/(1 - m u). [PDF p. 2, printed p. 784, equation (1.2), error definition, and finite-product display; PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, pairwise definition and equation (3.6)] If all inputs are nonnegative and their exact sum is nonzero, combining this bound with the paper's R_n = 1 observation yields relative error at most gamma_{log_2 n}; this pairwise relative form is inferred rather than separately printed. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 785, relative-error display and nonnegative-input paragraph; PDF p. 6, printed p. 788, equation (3.6)]
